web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Ten-Year Financial Forensics — Cycles, Dilution & The Blackstone JV
question: What do ten years of audited income statements, cash flows, share counts, and non-controlling interest structures reveal about EQT's earnings quality, ROIC, and balance-sheet resilience?

epigraph.quote: A decade of 10-Ks strips away every cyclical illusion; what remains is cumulative free cash flow, return on invested capital, and the diluted share count.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Ledger

web_blocks.html: A ten-year review from FY2016 through FY2025 captures EQT's shift across two regimes [1, 16, 17]. The pre-2019 era brought the $6.7 billion Rice Energy deal, large write-downs, and negative free cash flow [1, 16, 17]. The post-2019 Rice era rebuilt unit costs and cash generation [1, 16]. Over the decade, revenue grew from $1,387 million in FY2016 to $8,644 million in FY2025 [1]. Diluted shares rose from 167.0 million to 615.7 million, a 3.69x jump driven by stock deals for Rice Energy, Tug Hill, Equitrans, and Olympus [1, 13, 14, 17].

web_blocks.takeaway: EQT's P&L shows stark cyclicality—four consecutive GAAP net losses from 2018 to 2021—followed by structural cash-flow transformation in 2022–2025 as lower unit costs and midstream ownership took hold [1].

web_blocks.html: Three forensic points stand out in EQT's filings. First, look at GAAP Net Income vs. Cash Flow Conversion. In FY2025, EQT turned $2,326 million of consolidated net income ($2,039 million attributable to EQT) into $5,126 million of operating cash flow [1]. That is a 2.20x CFO-to-net-income ratio, lifted by $2,600.4 million of non-cash DD&A [1]. In the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow hit $5,186.3 million, up from $4,000.6 million in 9M 2025 [5]. That shows strong cash conversion even as Q3 2026 revenue dipped 9.6% year-over-year to $1,770 million on summer shut-ins [5].

Second, look at Derivative & Impairment Accounting. EQT's FY2021 GAAP net loss of -$1,143 million came during a rising gas market [1]. Mark-to-market losses on legacy swap hedges hit revenue before physical gas was delivered [1]. By contrast, in FY2025, EQT booked $291.0 million in net hedge gains inside its $8,644.2 million revenue line [1]. Analysts must strip out unrealized hedge marks to see true EBITDA ($5.9 billion in FY2025) and cash margins [1].

Third, check The Blackstone Joint Venture (PipeBox LLC) & Balance Sheet Quality. In November 2024, EQT sold a 49% non-controlling stake in PipeBox LLC to Blackstone Credit & Insurance for $3.5 billion in cash [1, 10]. PipeBox holds MVP Series A and FERC-regulated transmission and storage assets [1, 10]. EQT kept operating control and still consolidates the JV on its balance sheet [1, 10]. Thus, FY2025 consolidated net income ($2,326 million) includes ~$287 million for non-controlling interests, leaving $2,039 million for EQT common holders [1]. Rating agencies S&P and Fitch watch PipeBox's cash waterfall closely because it carries preferred-like payouts [19]. Even so, both agencies lifted EQT's outlook to positive in 2026 [19]. Total debt fell from $9.36 billion at year-end 2024 to $7.85 billion at year-end 2025, then to $5.6 billion ($5.5 billion net debt; $5.22 billion senior notes) by September 30, 2026 [1, 5, 19].

Finally, check Capital Efficiency (ROIC vs. WACC). Trailing twelve-month ROIC sits near 8.56%, with ROE at 10.92% and Debt/Equity down to 0.22x [1]. That roughly matches an 8%–9% cost of capital for an investment-grade energy major [1]. Even the lowest-cost gas major earns modest mid-cycle returns on capital once you include deal goodwill and depletion. Entry discipline and cash returns therefore matter just as much as rock quality.

web_blocks.title: Forensic Flag: 3.69x Share Dilution Over the Decade
paragraphs: EQT's diluted share count rose from 167.0M in FY2016 to 615.7M in FY2025—and will expand further upon closing the all-stock Range Resources merger (where Range holders receive 27% of the combined company) [1, 6]. Future per-share compounding depends on retiring shares or growing FCF/share faster than M&A equity issuance.

web_blocks.html: Debt reduction from 2024 through Q3 2026 shows how fast EQT repaired its balance sheet after buying Equitrans [1, 5, 19]. At year-end 2024, total debt was $9,360 million after peaking near ~$14 billion intra-year [1, 19]. Using $3.5 billion from the Blackstone JV, $1.25 billion from non-operated asset sales, and organic free cash flow, EQT cut total debt to $7,850 million by year-end 2025 [1, 10, 19]. In early 2026, EQT also ran cash tender offers upsized above $1.4 billion [19]. Senior notes fell from $6,933.2 million at year-end 2025 to $5,219.6 million at September 30, 2026 [1, 5]. That brought total debt to $5.6 billion and net debt to $5.5 billion [5].

Working capital ratios reflect normal E&P seasonality rather than stress. EQT's current ratio (~0.71x) looks tight on a single snapshot, yet that is normal for gas majors [1]. Gas sits underground as long-term reserves rather than current inventory, while receivables collect fast and credit lines stay undrawn [1]. Against $5.9 billion of FY2025 EBITDA, year-end 2025 total debt of $7.85 billion was ~1.33x EBITDA [1]. By Q3 2026, total debt of $5.6 billion sat below 1.0x run-rate EBITDA [5]. That low leverage supports investment-grade ratings and S&P's positive outlook revision in 2026 [1, 5, 19].

book_paragraphs: Numbers do not lie, especially when you lay ten years of Form 10-Ks side by side. If you and I look at EQT's decade from 2016 through 2025, we see two completely different companies living under the same ticker. The first company—from 2016 to 2021—looked like a value trap: four straight years of GAAP net losses from 2018 through 2021, heavy asset impairments, and derivative losses that confused even seasoned energy analysts [1].

The second company—from 2022 through 2026—is a cash-conversion powerhouse. Look at FY2025: revenue hit $8,644 million, operating income reached $3,250 million, and net income attributable to EQT was $2,039 million [1]. Yet operating cash flow was $5,126 million—more than double attributable net income—because EQT wrote off $2,600 million in non-cash depletion and depreciation [1]. That cash gusher continued into 2026, with nine-month operating cash flow reaching $5,186 million through September 30 [5].

Now let us put on our forensic accountant's visor and check three things that casual readers miss. First, watch the non-controlling interest line. When EQT formed the PipeBox LLC joint venture with Blackstone in November 2024 for $3.5 billion in cash, Blackstone took a 49% non-controlling stake [10]. That is why FY2025 consolidated net income was $2,326 million while EQT's common shareholders kept $2,039 million—roughly $287 million went to Blackstone's share of the midstream pipes [1]. It was a brilliant trade to slash senior debt down to $5.6 billion by Q3 2026 [5], but you must never double-count that 49% midstream cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Share Count, ROIC, and the Verdict on Business Quality
paragraphs: Second, look at the diluted share count. In FY2016, EQT had 167.0 million diluted shares; by FY2025, it had 615.7 million—a 3.69x increase [1]. And when the Range Resources all-stock merger closes in early 2027, Range shareholders will own 27% of the combined enterprise [6]. Yes, EQT bought extraordinary assets with that stock, but equity dilution is permanent.

Third, look at return on invested capital. At roughly 8.6% ROIC on trailing figures, EQT earns right around its cost of capital across a normal gas cycle. That tells you and me everything we need to know about the business quality verdict: EQT is the undisputed operational champion of North American dry gas, with peer-leading ~$2.00/MMBtu breakevens and a fortress 0.22x debt-to-equity ratio [3, 6]. Yet it remains a cyclical business whose long-term compounding depends on commodity discipline, LNG export margins, and proving that mega-mergers translate into rising free cash flow per share.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Cash flow conversion of 2.2x net income and a $5.6B debt balance prove EQT's balance sheet is battle-ready. Still, an 8.6% ROIC and 3.69x decade-long share expansion remind us that even the lowest-cost driller cannot escape commodity cyclicality.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing the Current Ratio and the Credit Upgrade
paragraphs: If you glance at EQT's balance sheet ratios without context, one number might make you blink: a current ratio around 0.71x. In a retail or manufacturing business, a current ratio below 1.0x can signal a working-capital crunch. In an upstream natural gas major, it is completely normal.

Why? Because EQT does not keep billions of dollars of finished goods sitting in a warehouse classified as 'current inventory.' Its inventory sits seven thousand feet underground in the Marcellus Shale, booked under long-term oil and gas properties. Meanwhile, EQT collects cash from utilities and pipelines every thirty days while carrying normal accounts payable and accrued drilling costs.

What actually matters for solvency is debt-to-EBITDA and maturity walls. By slashing senior notes from $6.93 billion at year-end 2025 down to $5.22 billion by September 30, 2026—and cutting total debt to $5.6 billion against nearly $5.9 billion of FY2025 EBITDA—EQT brought leverage under 1.0x [1, 5]. That is why credit agencies like S&P shifted EQT's outlook to positive in 2026 [19], and why the balance sheet is structurally prepared to absorb Range Resources without taking on new acquisition debt [6].

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Forensics: PipeBox JV, Dilution & Earnings Quality
paragraphs: Whenever an energy company executes back-to-back transformational deals—Equitrans Midstream in 2024 and Range Resources in 2026—a forensic analyst must look straight past adjusted EBITDA and inspect three things: true cash conversion, off-balance-sheet or JV commitments, and share count dilution.

First, EQT's cash conversion is genuine: FY2025 operating cash flow exceeded net income comfortably, and free cash flow reached $2,802 million. Second, the Blackstone PipeBox midstream joint venture was a clever de-leveraging tool that brought in upfront cash to retire high-cost acquisition debt, though it does carve out a non-controlling interest slice of midstream cash flows that we explicitly account for in enterprise value.

Third, share dilution is the one blemish on EQT's ten-year forensic scorecard. Between the 2017 Rice Energy merger, the 2024 Equitrans stock deal, and other equity issuances, EQT's share count expanded 3.69x from FY2016 to FY2025—and the pending Range Resources merger will issue another ~27% in new equity. Equity-funded M&A protected the balance sheet from Chesapeake-style bankruptcy, which was the right survival choice, but it means per-share compounding now depends on retiring shares or driving real per-share FCF growth post-2027.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing the Balance Sheet for a Multi-Year Gas Trough
paragraphs: Let us run a quick balance-sheet stress test together. Suppose Henry Hub averages $2.25 per MMBtu for two straight years—a severe cyclical slump. With $5.5 billion of net debt against an investment-grade maturity ladder and a ~$2.00 per MMBtu unlevered breakeven, EQT remains cash-flow positive before discretionary growth capex, aided by its hedged collar book and fee-based midstream earnings.

That resilience stands in stark contrast to the 2012–2020 Chesapeake Energy failure base rate we examined in Chapter 1. EQT's balance sheet is built to survive the trough; the only open question for equity holders is whether post-2027 free cash flow goes toward retiring the shares issued in the Equitrans and Range Resources deals.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Ten years of audited filings reveal a company that cured its operational and balance-sheet fragility, leaving commodity cycle timing and M&A integration as the primary remaining variables.
